sources.title: Existing Boracay weather page – legacy beach marker dataset
sources.publisher: PH project repository
sources.limitations: Coordinates and broad coast classifications were carried over from the existing weather page. These are legacy map markers, not independently surveyed beach centroids or verified boundary points.

sources.title: Boracay Map – Tourism Promotions Board Philippines
sources.publisher: Tourism Promotions Board Philippines
sources.limitations: The PDF identifies itself as a tourist map, says it must not be used as an official reference, and states information was accurate as of April 2020. Its Beach / Dive Site index supports map labels and grid references only; it does not establish surveyed beach boundaries, exact centroids, current access, or present-day conditions.

sources.title: Recreational Waters Monitoring Program: Annual Water Quality Assessment Report, Boracay Island, January–December 2022
sources.publisher: DENR Environmental Management Bureau Region VI
coverage: Ilig-Iligan Shell Museum sampling station coordinates
Annual fecal-coliform geomean and compliance statistics for 2022
2022 quarterly oil-and-grease averages and compliance statistics for monitored stations
Ralph's Place station water-quality results; linked to Bulabog Beach by SRC-010
sources.limitations: Historical monitoring data from January–December 2022. Sampling stations are not necessarily co-located with the whole beach; station coordinates must not be treated as beach centroids. Fecal-coliform results cover 12 sampling events; oil-and-grease monitoring was quarterly (April, June, September and November). Results must not be presented as current water quality or current bathing safety.

sources.title: Environmental Performance Report and Management Plan – Boracay Island Water Supply System Project

sources.limitations: Report describes monitoring station locations and historical water quality; not a real-time beach safety bulletin.

sources.title: Assessment of Benthic Macrofauna and Sediment Characteristics of Boracay Island, Philippines
sources.publisher: Sustainable Aquatic Research; University of the Philippines Visayas authors
sources.limitations: Field sampling was conducted in October 2022 at three White Beach stations only. It does not provide surveyed beach boundaries, beach width/slope, bathymetry, or a current island-wide ecological status. Station coordinates are research sampling points, not beach centroids.

sources.title: Regional State of the Brown Environment Report 2021 – Western Visayas
sources.publisher: DENR Environmental Management Bureau Region VI
coverage: Ralph's Place regular ambient monitoring station
Lapuz-Lapuz Beach historical ambient monitoring station coordinates
CY 2006–2019 historical station table: Lapuz-Lapuz Beach
CY 2006–2019 historical Bulabog Beach station at a different coordinate
CY 2020-onwards station table: Ralph's Place with station name Bulabog Beach
sources.limitations: The report contains two distinct station inventories: Table 4.53 covers CY 2006–2019, while Table 4.54 covers CY 2020 onwards. Table 4.53 lists Lapuz-Lapuz Beach and an older Bulabog Beach station at 11°56′08″N, 121°55′39″E. Table 4.54 lists Ralph's Place as a regular ambient station with the station name Bulabog Beach at 11°58′09.0″N, 121°55′38.4″E. These records must not be conflated. The report supports station identity and historical metadata, not beach boundaries or current water quality.

sources.title: 2023 Regional State of the Brown Environment Report – Western Visayas
sources.publisher: Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Environmental Management Bureau Region VI
coverage: Boracay Island coastal and marine water-quality monitoring stations
2023 regular monitoring station inventory, water-body classes and DMS coordinates (Table 4.50)
sources.limitations: Station-specific annual results, not whole-beach measurements or current real-time bathing-water advice. The fecal-coliform compliance chart caption states Jan–Nov 2023 while report narrative refers to 12 sampling events; sampling-event count is therefore not copied. The report contains conflicting 2023 TSS values for Ralph's Place (32.3 and 33.4 mg/L); that TSS value is excluded. Station inventory confirms names, classes and coordinates; it does not independently prove every sampling event used the same field position beyond the published station record.

sources.title: 2024 Regional State of the Brown Environment Report – Western Visayas
sources.publisher: Department of Environment and Natural Resources, Environmental Management Bureau Region VI
coverage: Boracay coastline and inland wetland water-quality programme
sources.limitations: The official PDF is indexed and confirms January–July 2024 Boracay water-quality data were presented to BIWQMACA, but the PDF could not be retrieved for full table validation during this research pass. The EMB Region 6 WQMA page currently links the Boracay Annual Assessment Report 2022. No station-level numeric values for 2024 are transcribed from this source.

sources.title: DENR-EMB says Boracay waters within safe standards
sources.publisher: Manila Bulletin, reporting statements by DENR-EMB Region VI
sources.limitations: Reports an EMB statement that all 24 monitoring stations passed water-safety tests during January–June 2024. No station-specific numeric values or full station list are supplied; this is historical island-level context, not a current beach-specific bathing-water result.

sources.title: Boracay outfalls pass initial water quality tests
sources.publisher: Daily Tribune, reporting EMB Region VI monitoring activity
sources.limitations: Reports compliant in-situ dissolved oxygen, temperature and pH at four outfalls. TSS, color and fecal-coliform samples had been sent for laboratory analysis and results were pending at publication. Outfalls are not beach bathing-water monitoring stations; no beach-specific safety conclusion is supported.

sources.title: Executive Order No. 53 – Creating a Boracay Inter-Agency Task Force
sources.publisher: Office of the President of the Philippines; Supreme Court E-Library
coverage: Enforcement of the 25+5 meter beach easement
sources.limitations: Directs DENR to enforce and monitor the 25+5 meter easement established under existing laws, rules and regulations. Does not identify or verify public approach routes to individual beaches.

sources.title: Presidential Decree No. 1067 – Water Code of the Philippines, Article 51
sources.publisher: Supreme Court E-Library
coverage: Public-use easement along shores of seas and lakes
Recreation, navigation, floatage, fishing and salvage
sources.limitations: Article 51 establishes a public-use easement whose width depends on the relevant area classification. It does not by itself establish the current physical approach route or access status for a particular named beach.

sources.title: DENR Administrative Order No. 2021-07 – Guidelines on the Establishment of Legal Easements Along the Seas, Rivers, Lakes, Esteros, and Creeks
sources.publisher: Department of Environment and Natural Resources
sources.limitations: General national rules; land classification and any protected-area designation must be verified for the specific shoreline segment before assigning a width or access status.

sources.title: DENR Clarifies Prohibitions in Boracay
sources.publisher: Department of Environment and Natural Resources
coverage: Restrictions on structures and activities within the easement
sources.limitations: Explains restrictions within the 25+5 easement area; does not establish current access routes or access permission at each beach.

sources.title: DENR 2020 Annual Report – Boracay Rehabilitation Program
sources.publisher: Department of Environment and Natural Resources
coverage: 2020 Boracay coastal and marine resource assessment
Coral assessment, fish visual census and seagrass survey
Mapping and delineation of coastal and marine resources and marine protected areas
sources.limitations: Confirms that mapping and delineation results were presented to stakeholders on 30 September 2020. The cited section does not provide the MPA boundary coordinates or a legal instrument establishing each mapped area.

sources.title: New seagrass species found in Boracay
sources.publisher: Manila Bulletin, reporting DENR Region VI mapping findings
sources.limitations: Reports 95.37 ha seagrass bed, nine species, and barangay-level cover figures from a mapping report described as subject to regional review. These are historical island/barangay aggregates, not beach-specific values or current condition.

sources.title: Coral Triangle Initiative Annual Report 2020
sources.publisher: Coral Triangle Initiative
coverage: Boracay coastal and marine resource assessment
Coral reef, seagrass and mangrove mapped extent
sources.limitations: Records approximately 763 ha coral reefs, 95.37 ha seagrass and 1.90 ha mangroves from the 2020 mapping assessment. These are island-wide mapped extents, not live coral cover or beach-level condition.

sources.title: Aklan's underwater treasures reveal rich marine biodiversity
sources.publisher: Daily Guardian, reporting DENR PENRO Aklan and DENR Region VI
coverage: DENR PENRO habitat validation and mapping in 2024–2025
sources.limitations: Reports 763.30 ha of coral habitat for Boracay within a province-wide 1,884.54 ha inventory. Area extent is not live coral cover, reef health, or a beach-specific assessment. The article does not provide mapped polygon coordinates.

sources.title: Protected Area Information System – Aklan Province
sources.publisher: DENR Biodiversity Management Bureau
coverage: Encoded protected-area records for Aklan Province
sources.limitations: The retrieved province page did not surface a Boracay-specific protected-area record. PAIS is based on encoded records and its dashboard warns that updates and validation may be incomplete; absence from the retrieved page is not proof that no protected-area designation exists.

sources.title: Protected Area Information System – Data Disclaimer
sources.publisher: DENR Biodiversity Management Bureau
coverage: PAIS dashboard data currency and validation limitations
sources.limitations: The dashboard states that data may not fully reflect actual or real-time conditions while updates and validation are ongoing. It cannot alone support a definitive negative finding for a specific location.

sources.title: DOST-PAGASA Climate Advisories – Monsoon Overview
sources.publisher: Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration
coverage: General seasonal monsoon definitions for the Philippines
sources.limitations: Defines the broad national monsoon wind directions, not local Boracay wind speed, wave height, nearshore currents or beach-specific sea state. Used only with coarse coast orientation to describe a provisional directional exposure inference.

sources.title: NAMRIA – Provision of Free Printed or Digital Data / Hydrographic and Bathymetric Products
sources.publisher: National Mapping and Resource Information Authority
coverage: Bathymetry charts and ASCII XYZ bathymetry data
Hydrographic smooth sheets for inshore ports and harbors
Raw/processed tidal current and wave data per month per station
sources.limitations: Catalogue confirms product availability/request channels, not the existence of a specific Boracay dataset or its values. No bathymetry, current or wave measurements are transcribed from this page.

sources.title: Philippine Notices to Mariners – Monthly Edition 2026-04
sources.publisher: National Mapping and Resource Information Authority
coverage: Chart 1544 – Panay Island NW Coast, Potol Point to Boracay Island
Submarine pipeline chart correction; affected ENCs PH5CATIC and PH2CVZ40
sources.limitations: The notice gives separate coordinate pairs for charts 1544 and 4358; they must be retained as chart-specific representations, not silently merged. The pipeline correction is a navigation-chart feature, not a beach boundary or automatically defined recreational exclusion zone.

sources.title: List of Available Electronic Navigational Charts as of 13 February 2025
sources.publisher: National Mapping and Resource Information Authority
sources.limitations: Confirms chart availability only; does not provide chart depth values or a downloadable chart extract in the retrieved listing.

sources.title: Elemental and Isotopic Techniques to Trace the Nutrient Sources in the Neritic Zone and Provenance of White Beach Sand of Boracay Island, the Philippines
sources.publisher: Philippine Journal of Science; Philippine Nuclear Research Institute, Department of Science and Technology
coverage: Approximate length and setting of White Beach
Offshore reef and seagrass presence at Bulabog
Neritic-zone sampling sites and historical water-quality context
sources.limitations: The article describes White Beach as approximately 4 km and Bulabog as approximately 2.5 km. It describes an offshore reef and seagrass beds at Bulabog, but does not provide beach-boundary or reef-polygon coordinates. Field sampling described in the methods was conducted in 2011–2012; the article's publication year must not be mistaken for the sampling year.

sources.title: Boracay outfalls pass initial water quality tests
sources.publisher: Daily Tribune, reporting EMB Region VI
coverage: EMB-6 and BIWQMACA two-day outfall sampling on 2–3 March 2026
On-site DO, temperature and pH compliance; laboratory TSS, color and fecal-coliform samples pending
sources.limitations: Reports outfall samples, not ambient recreational-water stations or beach bathing points. No numerical values or coordinates are published; laboratory results for TSS, color and fecal coliform were pending at publication.

sources.title: DENR-EMB says Boracay waters within safety standards
sources.publisher: Manila Bulletin, reporting DENR-EMB Western Visayas
coverage: All 24 Boracay monitoring stations reported as passing the water-safety test
sources.limitations: No station-level values, individual parameter breakdown or sampling-site table is published in the article. Treat as a reported WQMA-level/monitoring-program summary, not a substitute for the 2024 RSoBER station tables.

sources.title: Philippine Development Report 2024 – Annexes
sources.publisher: Department of Economy, Planning, and Development
coverage: Boracay Island among three WQMAs reported to meet fecal-coliform guideline values
All 40 WQMAs reported compliant with pH and nitrate guideline values
sources.limitations: Aggregated WQMA-level performance, not individual Boracay station results or beach-specific water quality. Does not provide station names, numerical values or sampling dates for Boracay.
